doc.title: Christian McBride interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996

title: James Brown, Philly Soul and a bass-playing family
summary: The James Brown answering machine scream leads to growing up in 1970s Philadelphia with Philly Soul, an R&B bassist father and a bass-playing great uncle.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: We are filming this evening for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive. It’s a great pleasure to have Christian McBride join us, and for a hot set at the Sarasota Jazz Festival. I’m going to make a guess from listening to your answer machine a couple of times trying to reach you, that jazz was not your only influence when you were growing up.
That’s exactly right. You are referring to the scream you hear when my answer machine picks up, the scream of James Brown. Everyone seems to get awakened by that.
The first time I heard it.

James was my main man growing up in Philadelphia in the 70s, that’s what the hot thing was in Philadelphia, Philly Soul. And of course my parents listened. My father is a bass player and he played on the R & B circuit in the 70s so that’s definitely as much a part of me as is jazz.
It was in your blood, and was it your great uncle who also plays bass?
That’s right. So it was destined.
